title: SDK Client Policy Curator: default retry budgets, id-key ergonomics, and synthetic error harness for chunked streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a cross-SDK 'policy curator' that packages opinionated defaults for retry budgets, backoff profiles, and idempotency key ergonomics tailored to chunked/streaming workloads. Deliver an automated synthetic error harness that can exercise streaming resume, partial-response dedup, and quota-aware retry budgets to validate defaults across Python/TS/Go SDKs.
motivation: We have many ad-hoc retry configs in each SDK and recurring customer incidents around resumed streams and duplicate tokens. A single curated default policy plus a synthetic harness will reduce production surprises and give engineering and SDK maintainers empirical data to tune defaults without frequent breaking changes.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a documented default policy object for Python/TS/Go SDKs that includes: retry budget (token- and time-based), 3 backoff profiles (latency-sensitive, throughput-optimized, safety-conservative), and idempotency key guidance for streaming uploads and chunked responses.
SDKs accept the policy via a single config entry (e.g., Redwood.policyCurator.loadDefault()) with language idiomatic wrappers.

Synthetic error harness can run locally and in CI, injecting failure modes: transient 5xx, network partition (stream cut), truncated responses, delayed first-byte, and partial duplicate events. It must produce a reproducible scorecard (retry count distribution, duplicate suppression rate, latency impact).
Telemetry points (per-request retry_count, final_outcome, idempotency_key_used, stream_resume_count) are emitted and mapped to existing dashboards (link in attachments).
Backward-compatible: existing SDK users who don't opt-in keep current defaults; opt-in returns consistent behaviour across SDKs.
technical_decisions: Retry budget model: hybrid token/time window. Default budget = 10 tokens per minute per-session with token costs: 1 for request, variable for resumed-chunk based on byte-size. Rationale: balances burst recovery vs runaway retries.
Backoff profiles: use jittered exponential with configurable min/max and capped retry attempts per profile. Latency-sensitive profile defaults to lower max attempts (3) and shorter base delay (50ms).

Idempotency keys: SDKs will auto-generate stable id-keys for streaming sessions (v1 format: sdkName:epoch:uuid) but allow callers to override. Keys rotate only on explicit session restart. This prevents accidental duplicate-processing on transient reconnects.
Transport hooks: expose granular hooks for the SDK transport layer to observe retry decisions for testing and telemetry without changing public API shapes.
implementation_notes: Add PolicyCurator module in each SDK repo. Python: redwood.sdk.policy_curator, TS: @redwood/sdk/policyCurator, Go: redwood/sdk/policycurator.
Create a canonical YAML policy spec in shared repo (redwood-infra/policy-spec) that the SDKs consume during build or CI verification.
Synthetic harness lives in infra/testing/stream-harness. It will run containerized agents that simulate server-side partial responses and client-side SDKs in a matrix across languages.
Map synthetic harness outputs to an approval gate: synthetic score must not regress by >5% for duplicate suppression when changing default budgets/backoff profiles.
risks: New defaults could inadvertently increase cost for high-throughput customers if budgets are too permissive—mitigate with telemetry and a conservative conservative profile.
Auto-generated id keys might collide with existing customer keys in edge cases—provide clear migration notes and an opt-out.
Complexity of harness might delay rollout; prioritize minimal viable harness for initial phase.
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy parsing and default generation in each SDK.
Integration tests: run synthetic harness matrix in CI for Python/TS/Go nightly for first 2 weeks after merge.
Manual QA: run harness against staging runtime under limited dedicated capacity to verify telemetry mapping and backend-surface behaviours.
Post-release canary: release opt-in flag to 5% of SDK traffic then 25% before wide rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): merge PolicyCurator and harness, document public API, add opt-in flag --policy=curator-default to SDKs.
Phase 2 (monitor): run opt-in in nightly rolling against internal integration tests and selected customers under SE coordination.
Phase 3 (gradual default): Flip default only after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and no regression in duplicate suppression or latency SLOs.
Rollback strategy: immediate opt-out toggle in SDK config plus server-side graceful fallback policy.
